note: China dynasty gaps (Han, Song, Ming, Qing) between existing Qin/Tang/1911/1949; Meiji Japan 1868; Cold War end hinge (Berlin Wall falls 1989—do not duplicate mo-berlin-wall 1961). Books only where a page opened this pass gave age and a clean-enough read. Attached Maples in the Mist to existing cn-tang-dynasty. No clean living book cleared for 1911 or 1949.
source: Britannica event pages for years (curl); Kirkus and Nosy Crow / British Museum for books

events.title: Han dynasty in China
events.yearNote: Britannica Han dynasty: the second great imperial dynasty of China (206 BCE–220 CE), after the Zhou dynasty; so thoroughly did the Han establish what was thereafter considered Chinese culture that ‘Han’ became the Chinese word denoting someone who is ethnically Chinese.
events.summary: The Han dynasty rules China for centuries and shapes much of what later ages call Chinese culture.
context: Follows Qin unification on the short China arc.
History stop, not a devotion book.

events.title: Song dynasty in China
events.yearNote: Britannica Song dynasty: (960–1279), Chinese dynasty that ruled during one of its most brilliant cultural epochs; commonly divided into Bei (Northern) and Nan (Southern) Song; after 1127 the dynasty ruled only in South China.
events.summary: The Song dynasty rules China in a long stretch known for culture, learning, and trade, later only in the south.
context: Slots after Tang on the China arc; Mongol rule follows at the end of Song.

events.title: Ming dynasty in China
events.yearNote: Britannica Ming dynasty: Chinese dynasty that lasted from 1368 to 1644 and provided an interval of native Chinese rule between eras of Mongol and Manchu dominance; China exerted immense cultural and political influence on East Asia.
events.summary: Native Chinese rule returns under the Ming after Mongol rule. Cities, crafts, and sea voyages mark the age.
context: Re-opened Britannica this pass; Ming was verified last pass and held for the event cap.
Follows the Mongol Empire node chronologically at the dynasty’s start.

events.title: Qing dynasty in China
events.yearNote: Britannica Qing dynasty: the last of the imperial dynasties of China, spanning the years 1644 to 1911/12. Under the Qing the territory of the empire and its population grew significantly.
events.summary: The Qing are China’s last imperial dynasty. Their rule ends when the 1911 revolution creates a republic.
context: Leads into the existing Chinese Revolution of 1911 node.
Manchu dynasty; keep the kid summary plain.

events.title: Meiji Restoration
events.yearNote: Britannica Meiji Restoration: the political revolution in 1868 that brought about the final demise of the Tokugawa shogunate; the overthrow itself consisted of a coup d’état in Kyōto on January 3, 1868. Transformed Japan from an isolated feudal society into a modern industrialized state.
events.summary: Japan’s old shogun government is overthrown. The emperor’s new Meiji government begins to remake Japan into a modern state.
context: Regime change and rapid reform. Keep the kid summary short.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.yearNote: Britannica Berlin Wall: the border between East and West Germany was opened on November 9, 1989, following anti-government protests in East Germany; on November 9 the East German government opened the wall. Barrier period given as 1961 to 1989. (Do not confuse with mo-berlin-wall, the 1961 building of the wall.)
events.summary: East Germany opens the Berlin Wall. Families cross. The Cold War’s hard European border begins to crack.
context: End hinge beside the existing 1961 wall node mo-berlin-wall.
A Night Divided already ships for the wall’s building; do not re-add it here.

books.title: Maples in the Mist: Children's Poems from the Tang Dynasty
books.author: Minfong Ho
books.blurb: Short Tang dynasty poems in English and Chinese, with Chinese-style watercolor pictures—poems children once learned while learning to read.

books.title: Find Tom in Time: Ming Dynasty China
books.author: Fatti Burke
books.blurb: British Museum search-and-find picture tour of Ming China: find Tom and his cat while spotting emperors, crafts, and festival scenes.

leftOff.title: Living book for Chinese Revolution of 1911 (cn-1911-revolution)
leftOff.why: No family-clean juvenile title with a parents’ or publisher age page opened this pass. Mao-era propaganda picture books and class-struggle readers are not suitable for this house.

leftOff.title: Living book for People’s Republic of China 1949 (cn-prc-1949)
leftOff.why: Same gap: overview textbooks and CCP-era children’s propaganda opened in search were not clean living books with verified ages for a Christian home. Omitted rather than invent.

leftOff.title: The Meiji Restoration and the Rise of Modern Japan
leftOff.author: Monique Avakian
leftOff.why: Kirkus nonfiction 12+: covers Perry, rebellion, then overseas imperialism and minimal WWII. Oldest independent reader here is 13; imperialism/WWII stretch and age band keep it off the default path.

leftOff.title: Commodore Perry in the Land of the Shogun
leftOff.author: Rhoda Blumberg
leftOff.why: CSM age 10+: brief sailors’ sexual interest ashore; ritual suicide; swordplay. Pre-Meiji (1853–54) and not clean enough for this house.

leftOff.title: Heart of a Samurai
leftOff.author: Margi Preus
leftOff.why: CSM age 10+: brutal whaling, drunken sailors threatening fishermen, ethnic slurs. Set 1841, before Meiji; left off.

leftOff.title: Brush of the Gods
leftOff.author: Lenore Look
leftOff.why: Penguin ages 4–8 verified (Tang painter Wu Daozi). Passed over Maples in the Mist as the cleaner Tang attach; Buddhist temple-art imagery (flying Buddhas) makes Maples the safer default for this house.

leftOff.title: The Magic Pillow
leftOff.author: Demi
leftOff.why: Kirkus picture book 7–9; Tang-dynasty folktale. Fine tone, but Maples already covers Tang with a clearer dynasty-poetry link; not doubled.

leftOff.title: Flight for Freedom
leftOff.author: Kristen Fulton
leftOff.why: Kirkus picture book 5–8; true 1979 hot-air-balloon escape from East Germany. Clean-ish, but it is not the 1989 fall hinge; A Night Divided already covers the wall node. Not forced onto mo-berlin-wall-falls.

leftOff.title: The Wall: Growing Up Behind the Iron Curtain
leftOff.author: Peter Sís
leftOff.why: CSM age 8+: Czechoslovakia Cold War memoir; riot, plane hijacking, imprisonment, death. Heavy for default; not specifically the Berlin Wall fall of 9 November 1989. Left off rather than stretch.

leftOff.title: Foundations of Chinese Civilization (Understanding China through Comics)
leftOff.author: Jing Liu
leftOff.why: Covers into the Han, but the volume frames from the Yellow Emperor at 2697 BCE—deep-time prehistory this house does not want as doctrine. Omitted.

leftOff.title: Han / Song living books beyond dynasty cards
leftOff.why: No separate Han or Song title cleared this pass with both a clean parents’/publisher age page and household content rules (Emperor’s Painting Capstone page 404’d; 99 Questions About the Song Dynasty not opened to a stable age/source page).

leftOff.title: Cold War start as its own node
leftOff.why: Britannica Cold War Quick Facts Date 1947–1991, but the article also says the rivalry solidified by 1947–48—not a single hinge day. Per brief, preferred end hinge used instead (fall of the Berlin Wall).
